candidate_concepts.label: Bag-of-Words Model Definition
candidate_concepts.description: The BOW model represents text as fixed-length vectors by counting the frequency of each word in the document. It disregards grammar and word order.
coverage_criteria: Explain what BOW model is and how it represents text.
Identify that BOW outputs a vector of word counts.

extraction_reason.source_grounded_rationale: The article explicitly defines BOW as 'representation that turns arbitrary text into fixed-length vectors by counting how many times each word appears'.
extraction_reason.granularity_rationale: This is a foundational concept; students can be asked to define and give an example.

source_anchors.locator: A Simple Explanation of the Bag-of-Words Model

candidate_concepts.label: Vocabulary in Bag-of-Words
candidate_concepts.description: The vocabulary is the set of all unique words present in the document corpus. It forms the dimensions of the BOW vectors.
coverage_criteria: Given a set of documents, identify the vocabulary.

extraction_reason.source_grounded_rationale: The article defines vocabulary as 'the set of all words found in our document set' and shows how it determines vector dimensions.
extraction_reason.granularity_rationale: This is a specific component of BOW; checking this ensures understanding of vectorization.

candidate_concepts.label: BOW Vectorization Steps
candidate_concepts.description: To vectorize text with BOW, first determine the vocabulary (unique words), then count occurrences of each word in each document to form a vector.
coverage_criteria: List the two steps of BOW vectorization.
Apply counting to a simple example.

extraction_reason.source_grounded_rationale: The article walks through 'Step 1: Determine the Vocabulary' and 'Step 2: Count' with an example.
extraction_reason.granularity_rationale: This is a procedural concept; students can be asked to perform the steps on new text.

candidate_concepts.label: Context Loss in Bag-of-Words
candidate_concepts.description: BOW model loses word order and contextual information, functioning like a literal bag of words: only word presence/frequency counts, not position.
coverage_criteria: Explain why BOW ignores word order.
Describe the trade-off of using BOW (simplicity vs context loss).

extraction_reason.source_grounded_rationale: The article states 'Notice that we lose contextual information... It's like a literal bag-of-words: it only tells you what words occur... not where they occurred.'
extraction_reason.granularity_rationale: Understanding limitations is key; a single question can confirm this concept.

source_anchors.locator: Notice that we lose contextual information, e.g. where in the document the word appeared, when we use BOW. It's like a literal bag-of-words: it only tells you what words occur in the document, not where they occurred.

candidate_concepts.label: BOW Implementation with Keras Tokenizer
candidate_concepts.description: BOW can be implemented in Python using Keras' Tokenizer class: fit_on_texts to build vocabulary, then texts_to_matrix with mode='count' to get count vectors.
coverage_criteria: Explain how to use Tokenizer for BOW.
Write code to fit tokenizer and get count matrix.

extraction_reason.source_grounded_rationale: The article provides a code example using Keras Tokenizer, demonstrating fit_on_texts and texts_to_matrix with count mode.
extraction_reason.granularity_rationale: This is a practical implementation detail that can be checked with code-oriented questions.

candidate_concepts.label: Applications and Strengths of Bag-of-Words
candidate_concepts.description: BOW is used in NLP tasks like Text Classification and profanity detection due to its simplicity and low computational cost, despite losing context.
coverage_criteria: Explain why BOW is useful despite its simplicity.

extraction_reason.source_grounded_rationale: The article mentions 'often used for Natural Language Processing (NLP) tasks like Text Classification' and a blog post for profanity detection, and states its strengths: simplicity, inexpensive to compute.
extraction_reason.granularity_rationale: This concept ties the technique to real-world use; questions can ask about when BOW is appropriate.
